items.title: Off-duty Sudbury police sergeant charged with assault after incident at Mississauga hotel
items.summary: A sergeant with Greater Sudbury Police Service’s Intimate Partner Violence Unit has been charged with assault by Peel Regional Police in connection with an alleged off-duty incident in southern Ontario earlier this month. Peel police said officers responded to an altercation at a hotel in Mississauga on Nov. 7. “As a result of the investigation, 40-year-old Jeffrey Mussen was charged with assault and 48-year-old Matthew Bedard was charged with uttering threats to cause death or bodily harm,” Peel Regional Police wrote in an email to CTV News. According to Peel police, both men were released at the scene and are scheduled to appear in court at a later date. “The Greater Sudbury Police Service is aware that Jeffrey Mussen has been charged with assault by Peel Region Police in relation to an alleged off-duty incident that occurred in Southern Ontario,” said Kaitlyn Dunn, the service’s corporate communications supervisor, in an email to CTV News. Dunn said it would be inappropriate for the service to comment on the specific circumstances of the allegation, as the matter is before the courts and occurred outside its jurisdiction. ” Sudbury police said allegations of criminal conduct are addressed through the appropriate legal and internal processes.

items.title: Police on scene for ‘person in crisis’ at Mississauga apartment
items.summary: ” The ongoing incident happened at an apartment building on Fergus Avenue in Mississauga on Wednesday afternoon, Peel Regional Police say. Police say the incident is contained to a single unit, and that there are no safety concerns for residents in the area. There will be an “extended police presence” in the area, and police say building residents can speak with police officers on scene if they are unsure about access to the property. items.title: Plan to build $500M transit facility to house buses moves forward in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga is taking plans to build a new $500-million transit facility to the public next month as it looks to house its growing fleet of MiWay buses. , near Mississauga Road and Meadowvale Boulevard in the north end, remains among the municipality’s top priorities. The facility would be MiWay’s third transit garage. “The new facility will help expand transit services, grow the bus fleet and help move to zero-emission fleet technologies as part of the city’s Climate Change Action Plan,” Mississauga officials said in the update. MiWay, the City of Mississauga’s transit provider, currently keeps and repairs its 500 or so buses at two large facilities — one on Central Parkway West, in the Erindale area, and the other in Malton. However, those locations “are at full capacity, and we cannot add to our fleet without a new facility to maintain and operate (the new buses),” former mayor Carolyn Parrish said in a letter earlier this year to the federal government in which she asked, on the city’s behalf, for financial help in making a new MiWay transit operations, maintenance and storage facility a reality. “Based on preliminary designs and capacity projections, we need a site for 170 to 280 buses, with an estimated capital cost of more than $500 million,” the letter continued. “Without this new facility, our ability to advance zero-emission fleet adoption is significantly constrained. ” City officials said this week they’re hosting an open house on Dec. 8 to inform members of the public of their plans for the new transit facility.

items.title: Inquest into fatal Mississauga police shooting shown videos from after incident
items.summary: A police officer who helped pull a critically injured Black man from a wrecked car after a police shooting nearly seven years ago faced questions Wednesday about the time it took to call for medical treatment. Const. Marc Charlebois, then a member of Peel regional police’s tactical unit, arrived at the Mississauga townhouse complex about 20 minutes after the shooting, he told a coroner’s inquest into the death of Jamal Francique. Charlebois heard an officer had shot at a car during an attempted arrest, and that nobody could see inside the vehicle because it was dark outside and the car’s windows were tinted, he said. The constable told the inquest earlier this week that he knew after he broke the car’s rear passenger window that there had been a “traumatic incident” requiring intervention. He saw blood and could hear Francique’s agonal breathing, a type of laboured breath that indicates serious medical distress, he said. Charlebois also wrote in his notes that he saw signs of trauma to the right side of Francique’s head at that time, the inquest heard. After watching videos from the scene on Wednesday, however, Charlebois said he now believed he did not realize Francique had suffered a traumatic injury until he broke a second window, the one on the rear driver’s side. He made the inference based on his body language in the footage, he said. Several lawyers pushed back during cross-examination, arguing Charlebois would have known Francique was in grave condition based on his breathing alone. The officer told Ontario’s police watchdog that he could immediately hear Francique was in respiratory distress after breaking the first window but wasn’t sure if the man was faking it, they noted. Karifa Magassouba, a lawyer for the Black Action Defence Committee, argued Charlebois had other information that suggested it was a medical emergency, including the damage to the car and the knowledge that an officer had shot at the vehicle.

items.title: Neighbourhood park about to be completely transformed in Mississauga
items.summary: Residents in west Mississauga are being asked to help put the finishing touches on plans to completely redesign a neighbourhood park in their community. The City of Mississauga’s revised plan to enlarge and dramatically transform Bert Fleming Park will soon be put into motion pending one final public engagement session. Having updated an earlier blueprint for the park based on feedback from residents this past spring, city officials said this week their latest plan will now be put to the public test. “The updated plan includes changes to naturalization areas, park trails and open lawn areas, as well as an expanded children’s play area and community gathering spaces with seating,” the city said in a project update. Residents who want to provide feedback are being urged to look over details of the newest plan and complete an online survey by Dec. 14. Input from residents “will help transform Bert Fleming Park into a space that reflects the needs and priorities of the community,” project officials said. Not long ago fully surrounded by a traffic circle on The Credit Woodlands north of Dundas Street West and a couple blocks east of Mississauga Road, Bert Fleming Park is being redesigned to offer more amenities to residents and better connect them to the surrounding neighbourhood. Being completed through The Credit Woodlands Integrated Road Project, the park is also being enlarged by a half-acre, City of Mississauga staff said, adding new pedestrian crossings and sidewalks are also in the works.

items.title: Holiday campaign gives Mississauga residents a way to remember loved ones
items.summary: The holiday season is often a time for family gatherings and celebrations, but for people who have lost someone close to them, it can also be a difficult reminder of those who are no longer there. Hospice Mississauga is hoping to give residents a special way to remember loved ones while raising money for its programs and services through a new holiday campaign. The organization is launching its Trees of Remembrance campaign with a free community celebration on Thursday (Nov. 19) at Sherwood Village Mall (formerly Sheridan Mall, Eaton Sheridan Place and Sheridan Centre), a Mississauga shopping destination that first opened in 1969. m. , the Light Up the Holidays Social will feature decorated holiday trees, community activities and presentations. m. m. Residents will also have an opportunity to honour someone special by creating a personalized remembrance ornament. People can submit a message, cherished memory or tribute through the Hospice Mississauga website, and volunteers will prepare the ornaments and hang them on the trees. READ MORE: Construction begins on ‘much-needed’ $26M hospice facility in Mississauga The Trees of Remembrance campaign will continue Jan. 8, with trees sponsored and decorated by local businesses, community groups and individuals. The fundraising goal is $300,000, with the Longo Family Foundation offering to match holiday contributions up to $100,000.

items.title: City Urges Residents to Bookmark Favourites Ahead of Winter Program Registration
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents are being urged to register early for winter recreation and culture programs and March Break camps before popular spots fill up. The city says in a notice to residents that winter is a good time to learn something new, stay active and connect with the community, and that programs are open to all ages, interests and abilities. Officials are encouraging residents to browse Active Mississauga now and build a wish list by bookmarking programs ahead of registration opening in November for residents and in December for non-residents. The city reports in-person registration is also available at community centres during service desk hours for those who prefer not to book online. According to the city, the wish list approach helps residents move quickly once registration opens, with options for ages from preschoolers to older adults.

items.title: Dundas Street Pizza Pizza Reopens Same Day After Peel Health Ordered It Shut
items.summary: According to Peel Public Health, a Pizza Pizza location at 1093 Dundas St. W. in Mississauga was ordered closed during a Nov. 13 inspection but was allowed to reopen the same day. The health unit says inspectors routinely check local restaurants, cocktail bars, beverage rooms, bakeries and takeout food establishments to make sure they meet safety standards. Peel Public Health also issued conditional passes to several other food serving businesses and salons during recent rounds of inspections, according to the health unit. The outlet reports the closure order and conditional passes are part of the same routine inspection process that covers a wide range of Mississauga businesses. Peel Public Health notes these checks happen on an ongoing basis across the region, not only in response to complaints.

items.title: Brightwater Waterfront Project Marks New Groundbreaking as Unit Count Tops 3,800
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the Brightwater lakefront development in Mississauga reached another milestone this week with a new groundbreaking, as the developer highlighted the project's growth since construction began. The outlet reports Brightwater, at 70 Mississauga Rd. S. and 181 Lakeshore Rd., was approved in 2019 and broke ground in October 2021, with residents already living in the first two completed phases. Following approval of 898 additional units in late 2025, insauga.com reports the development now includes 3,893 residential units across apartments, townhouses and live work units. The site also includes a Farm Boy grocery store that opened in 2024, alongside other businesses now operating within the community. DiamondCorp president Ty Diamond said Brightwater has evolved from a long term vision into a vibrant waterfront community, according to insauga.com.

items.title: Provincial Deadline Pushes Mississauga to Finalize Heritage Status for Two Century-Old Buildings
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, city staff are recommending council designate two historic properties, a 1917 bungalow at 1 Godfrey's Lane in Port Credit and a 1908 building at 20 Thomas St. in Streetsville, as heritage sites despite objections from their owners. The outlet reports the recommendation goes before the city's general committee on Nov. 18 and stems from a provincial rule requiring heritage designation within two years of listing, or the city loses the ability to re-list a property for five years. Both buildings are already on the heritage registry, which only requires a 60 day demolition notice rather than full protection, mississauga.com reported. The bungalow's owners first objected in February 2024, leading council to defer its decision that September. The outlet notes the city has until Jan. 1, 2027 to act, and the documents provided disclose no redevelopment plans.

items.title: Developers to fight Mississauga’s data centre moratorium at Ontario Land Tribunal
items.summary: Two developers will fight Mississauga’s one-year pause on data centres at the Ontario Land Tribunal. Industrial real estate company Prologis and real estate developer Montcrest Asset Management have both filed appeals with the Ontario Land Tribunal over Mississauga’s temporary ban on large-scale data centres. A provincial body, the tribunal adjudicates matters related to land use planning and can override municipal decisions. Amid a public outcry, Mississauga councillors passed a bylaw effectively banning the construction of large-scale data centres for up to two years while the city studies the issue. Many communities have raised concerns about the massive centres’ potential water consumption, electricity use, noise and air quality. Data centres don’t require a large number of employees once they are constructed. Data centres have been around for decades, and are needed to store and process digital information such as Google Maps, online banking and social media. During the AI boom, the need for new centres has vastly increased. After Prologis proposed a two-storey data centre for vacant land they own on Tenth Line West in the Meadowvale Business Park, just south of Highway 401, the community packed into a community town hall. Over 200 people attended, and at times, the meeting got heated with frustrated residents trying to get questions answered. Montcrest doesn’t have a planning application for a data centre in Mississauga at this time, a City of Mississauga spokesperson told INSAUGA Canada. But Montcrest Asset Management owns eight acres of industrial land on Tahoe Boulevard near Toronto Pearson Airport.

items.title: Months-Long Investigation Into Bolton Shooting Leads to New Firearm Charges for Two Mississauga Men
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Caledon OPP have laid additional firearm charges against two Mississauga men after a monthslong investigation into a shooting at a Bolton home earlier this year. The outlet reports officers were called after reports of gunfire, and while no injuries were reported, a suspect vehicle described as a white Kia SUV was seen leaving the area. Police say the probe led them to execute two search warrants at a Mississauga residence on April 21 and May 28, seizing roughly six grams of cocaine along with items connected to drug trafficking. Charges were first laid in June, including unauthorized possession of a prohibited firearm, insauga.com reported. In the latest update, Pragash Segatheesan, 36, of Mississauga, was charged on Oct. 22 with trafficking in a firearm, according to the outlet.
